article.headline: Sean Longstaff hits double as Leeds stroll to victory over Coventry
article.description: Sean Longstaff scored twice and created another as Leeds beat Coventry 3-0 at Elland Road to seal a third successive top-flight win for the first time in five years.
article.linkText: Sean Longstaff hits double as Leeds stroll to victory over Coventry
article.story:
Sean Longstaff scored twice and created another as Leeds beat Coventry 3-0 at Elland Road to seal a third successive top-flight win for the first time in five years.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin celebrated signing his new contract this week by heading home the opening goal and Longstaff struck either side of the interval to keep Daniel Farke's side on an upward curve after last week's thumping win at Chelsea.

Leeds had not won three successive top-flight games since they ended the 2020-21 campaign under Marcelo Bielsa with a four-game winning run, while their fifth league win this season lifted them up to sixth in the table.

Ethan Ampadu and Jayden Bogle both fired off target from outside the penalty area, either side of a standing ovation for Gary Speed to mark the 15th anniversary of the former Whites midfielder's death.

But Leeds were back-pedalling when Sidiki Cherif raced on to a long ball over the top, forcing Nico Elvedi into a superb last-ditch tackle.

Leeds then began to stretch Coventry's defence. Noah Okafor fired wide and saw another shot blocked before Leeds forced a succession of corners without forcing Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth into a save.

James Justin was crowded out and Ampadu lashed over the crossbar from in front of goal.

The home side's pressure was rewarded though with two goals in four minutes just before halftime.

Longstaff's excellent free-kick was met by Calvert-Lewin's towering header -- the striker's sixth league goal of the season -- and the former Newcastle midfielder's shot took a big deflection off Tatsuhiro Sakamoto to wrong-foot Rushworth and put Leeds 2-0 up.

Leeds went close to increasing their lead early in the second period.

Calvert-Lewin was thwarted by Rushworth's diving save, Okafor curled a right-footed shot inches wide and Ao Tanaka's effort from the edge of the box span to safety after a deflection.

The third goal was brilliantly created by Gabriel Gudmundsson's back-heeled pass inside the box for Longstaff to sweep home his second in the 66th minute.

Rushworth's fine save with his legs denied Leeds a fourth after Calvert-Lewin's clever pass sent Bogle in one-on-one.

Leeds' rearguard had been rarely troubled by a Coventry side which had won four of their previous seven matches and Brandon Thomas-Asante's shot on the turn, which was well blocked by Elvedi, offered only temporary respite.

Home substitute Harry Wilson went close to his first Leeds goal with a curling effort from 20 yards and Calvert-Lewin's 77th-minute replacement Lukas Nmecha saw his angled shot blocked by Stephen Mfuni.
